question: A WhatsApp from an unknown number: Hi Mum, I dropped my phone in the loo. Who sent it?
answer: A scammer. The Hi Mum fraud, which spread through Britain and Australia in the early 2020s, needs no hacking: just a parent and a hurry. Nothing in the messages can expose it, since a real son with a broken phone would write the same. The urgency is there to stop the one check that can.
move: Check a story through a door you already had, never the one it offers.
ask: Who could reach me today with a story I would act on before checking?

clues.text: Hi Mum, dropped my phone in the loo. This is my new number x
Your daughter is beside you on the sofa, scrolling her own phone.
Can you pay a bill for me? My bank app won't work on this phone.
It has to go today. It's my flatmate's account, I'll pay you back x
You ring your son's old number. He answers at once, on the bus.

scene.why: Every message fitted a son with a broken phone. Only a call to the number you already had could.

reference: Action Fraud, UK National Fraud and Cyber Crime Reporting Centre, warnings on WhatsApp Hi Mum and Dad scams, 2022, https://www.actionfraud.police.uk
